learning_outcomes.text: Students will have knowledge of the concepts of descriptive and inductive statistics.

Students are able to identify, model, and solve statistical problems from business practice in the area of descriptive statistics using software tools such as spreadsheet programs (MS Excel, OpenOffice Calc, LibreOffice).

Students are able to solve practical statistical problems of inference from a sample to total populations using statistical techniques for parameter estimation, parametric hypothesis testing, and goodness-of-fit tests. They can create the necessary models with random variables, test functions, and their probability distributions, using software tools such as spreadsheet programs (MS Excel, OpenOffice Calc, LibreOffice).

syllabus_topics: The harmonic mean and the trimmed mean
Structure numbers, measure numbers, growth rates
Discrete probability distributions and distribution function
Continuous probability distributions and density function
Expected value and variance of a random variable
Tests for mean, proportion, standard deviation and differences
Point estimation methods: Method of moments
Parametric Hypothesis Tests with Small Samples
teaching_methods: Lectures using classical presentation techniques to convey theory and applications
Problem-solving with software tools for many concepts
Practice exercises for students' own work
Student presentations of solutions to selected exercises at the beginning of the next lecture
Discussion of student solution proposals in the iLearn system
assessment_rules: The module examination has a duration of 90 minutes. The grading weight is 5/210.
